column1: # The "signal peptide only" / "QUESTIONABLE" calls below were produced with a TRUNCATED
# 396 aa CHIT1 query. Human CHIT1 is 466 aa. Re-running with the full-length UniProt
# sequence aligns these same turtle proteins over 387-388 aa at 59.5-61.0%% identity
# (83%% query coverage, E = 0.0). They ARE full-length GH18 chitinase-family proteins.
# The conclusion that they are not CHIT1 ORTHOLOGS still stands, but rests on the
# phylogeny (Figure 5B), not on these similarity values.
# Human CHIT1 (Q13231) BLASTP vs turtle/tortoise genomes (NCBI nr, Testudines)
# Relaxed E-value cutoff: 1e-3 (hits shown below - all are signal-peptide-only matches)
# CRITICAL NOTE: All turtle "CHIT1-like" hits in NCBI are SIGNAL PEPTIDE MATCHES ONLY
# Alignment lengths: 34-44 aa out of 395 aa full-length CHIT1
# These are NOT true CHIT1 orthologs. They are GH18 family chitinase-like proteins
# that share only the N-terminal signal peptide region with CHIT1.
# - M. impressa: NO CHIT1 or CHIA found (no hits at E-value 1e-5 in local proteome BLAST)
# - All other turtles (22 species tested): NCBI annotations show "chitotriosidase-1-like" proteins,
#   BUT these only match the signal peptide region of human CHIT1 (35-36 aa / 395 aa = ~9% coverage).
# - These turtle proteins are likely GH18 family chitinase-like proteins (e.g., CHIA/AMCase-like)
#   that were AUTO-ANNOTATED as "chitotriosidase-1" due to shared N-terminal signal peptide similarity.
# - TRUE CHIT1 (full-length chitotriosidase with catalytic domain homology) appears to be ABSENT
#   from ALL tested turtle genomes, including M. impressa.
# - This is consistent with known biology: CHIT1 and CHIA are GH18 family members that share
#   signal peptide and some structural features but differ in substrate specificity and expression.
#   Turtles appear to have GH18 family members (annotated as chitinase-like) but lack true CHIT1.
